headline: P0002 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share of 18.4% against 2.8% expected for its patient mix, and the excess sits mostly on low-complexity patients, a pattern consistent with upcoding
rationale: P0002 billed 99215 on 46 of 250 claims (18.4%). Given its patients' complexity, about 2.8% would be expected (risk-adjusted score 5.40; z vs peers 1.98). The gap is not explained by a sicker panel. Most visits (151 of 250) were for patients with 0-1 chronic conditions. On those patients the provider's 99215 share was 18.0% and 21.8%, against 2.1% and 3.4% for all providers. For patients with 4+ conditions the share was 14.3%, close to the 13.9% norm. The sampled claims show 99215 billed for simple, single-problem visits on patients with no chronic conditions. Examples are an upper respiratory infection (C0000476, J06.9), a urinary tract infection (C0000524, C0000612, N39.0), low back pain (C0000437, C0000543, M54.50), rash (C0000462, C0000581, R21) and follow-up exams (C0000498, C0000562, Z09). There are also 99215s for single, often stable chronic conditions such as hypertension (C0000439, C0000485) and hyperlipidemia (C0000393). By contrast, the 99215s on a 4-condition patient with chronic kidney disease (C0000511, C0000631) look plausible. The sampled lower-level claims also lean high: 99214 for rash or follow-up on 0-condition patients (C0000505, C0000580). The billed mix is heavy at 99214 overall (149 of 250). These are random samples and there is no clinical documentation, so medical decision-making or time-based billing cannot be checked. Records could show acute complexity that the diagnosis codes do not capture.
next_steps: Request medical records for a sample of the 99215 claims on patients with 0-1 chronic conditions (e.g., C0000476, C0000612, C0000437, C0000498, C0000581). Check whether the documented medical decision-making or total time supports level 5.
Check whether the 99215s were billed on time and, if so, whether documented time meets the threshold for each encounter.
Review the 99214-heavy mix (149 of 250) for the same pattern on low-complexity patients, starting with C0000505 and C0000580.
Compare against the full claim set rather than the samples, including any modifiers, other services on the same day and place of service, to look for acuity the diagnosis codes do not capture.
Look at patients with repeated high-level visits over time (e.g., P0002-N0104, P0002-N0066) to see whether level selection is consistent with the documented reason for each visit.
